Workers' Rights Act
Workers' Rights Act

Section I of this bill sets the groundwork for fair compensation by establishing a minimum wage of 2.5 Sordish Ren per hour. This serves as a benchmark for fair and equitable pay, ensuring that no worker in Sordland is compensated below this rate. Section II addresses the issue of excessive labour, setting a maximum limit of 60 hours of work per week. This provision aims to prevent worker exploitation and safeguard the wellbeing of Sordish labour force. Section III introduces the concept of double overtime pay. This stipulates that any work performed beyond a 40-hour workweek will be compensated at twice the normal hourly wage. This incentivises fair work practices and ensures employees are duly compensated for their extended efforts. Section IV focuses on worker safety and humane work conditions. It mandates that employers must take all necessary steps to protect their workers from occupational hazards and ensure a dignified and safe working environment. This promotes a culture of respect and care within workplaces across Sordland. Section V extends these protections to migrant or undocumented workers, granting them the same rights as Sordish citizens. Employers who fail to abide by these rules will face substantial fines from the government, and persistent non-compliance will invite legal action. [-1 Government Budget]
The WRA bill has been passed by the GNA.
Agnolia Offshore Drilling Near Helji Increased Tensions

Agnolia has started a new oil drilling operation very close to the disputed territory of Heljiland. The tensions increased when the situation turned into a stand-off between Valgslandian and Agnolian warships.

It took several hours for the gridlock to be resolved and the situation was de-escalated for now.
President Walker Shows Full Support to Sordish Protestors

Arcasian President Dwight Walker has publicly aligned himself with the ongoing protests in Sordland, issuing a stern condemnation of the Sordish government. This declaration of support for the protestors and the explicit critique of the Sordish administration is seen as a direct response to Sordland's decision to sever diplomatic ties with Arcasia.
ATO Economic Summit in Perla: Capitalism's Diverse Forms

The ATO convened a pivotal summit in Perla, bringing together leaders and economic experts from member nations to address global economic developments and strategic responses. Discussions centered on the economic frameworks of Arcasian Capitalism and Lespian Protectionism within the alliance.

Arcasian Capitalism, characterized by market-oriented reform policies, deregulation, and privatization, maintains strong performance across ATO nations with an average GDP growth rate of 9.7% over the past decade, despite the inflation rate of 4.6% in the last year. The Lespian model, while preserving market principles, implements strategic protective measures through tariffs and targeted trade barriers, achieving an inflation rate of 1.8% and a GDP growth rate of 6.1%.

The summit facilitated integration discussions between these economic systems while respecting Lespia's firm stance on maintaining its distinct economic measures. This strategic dialogue addressed the CSP's expanding influence through state-owned enterprise (SOE) driven investment strategies across developing and emerging nations globally. 

The ATO continues to adapt its economic framework to support both competitive market dynamics and measured protections that safeguard member states' critical industries while preserving the alliance's market-oriented foundation.
Benfi Regional Airport Overcrowded

We have been receiving reports about the capacity of Benfi Regional Airport. The Mayor of Benfi is preparing to put a request forward for an investment to build an international airport in the city. For a touristic region like Benfi, he claims that it would increase the overall prosperity of Sordland.
Doctor's Strike

A thousand doctors and nurses were missing from hospitals in Benfi today in a strike to protest the health budget reduction. The PFJP mayor said that the strike has caused major disruptions with extended delays in services but agreed that their voice of concern was legitimate.

The Ministry of Health has been notified to identify the health workers and to ensure they return to work as soon as possible and to find alternative solutions to provide services in the meantime. Minister Beniwoll said that he will overcome the challenges presented.
Red Youth Members Charged With Terrorism and Treason

12 militants from the Red Youth have been tried and sentenced to 96 years in prison due to terrorism and treason related charges in Borin. Many more Red Youth members are waiting for their turn in prison. The Mayor of Borin reports concerns about reaching the maximum capacity of the prisons in region.
CSP Advocates Dissolution of Meftiem ITZ

The CSP has called for the dissolution of the Meftiem International Trade Zone. This strategic location in Morellan territory and complemented by a strategically vital port, has been the joint venture of Rizian, Morellan, Lespian, and Valgsland state corporations since the pre-revolutionary era. Yet, the recent ascension of Alma Saltana to the premiership of Morella has sparked a seismic shift in this arrangement. 

With staunch backing from Valgsland, Prime Minister Saltana has declared intentions to nationalize the mines and port, a move that potentially upends the status quo and alters the trajectory of the region's economic future. This move directly challenges the interests of Rizian Royal Gold and by extension, King Romus Toras of Rizia.

The announcement drew immediate attention from Lespia's Prime Minister Alvarez, an ATO stalwart, who firmly expressed his commitment to maintaining the current free market practices, heightening the tension between the two blocs.
United Contana Launches Second Satellite

In a significant technological milestone, United Contana has successfully launched a second satellite capable of facilitating radio communications. This development catapults United Contana to the forefront of space-based communication technology, enabling radio signals to be transmitted via satellite for the first time. 

No other nation currently possesses this advanced capability, marking a significant achievement for United Contana.
BFF Bombs Police Station

In a treacherous attack, the BFF has bombed a police station in Deyr. Initial casualties are reported at 3 officers dead and 22 injured. The perpetrators have escaped into the Gumren mountains near Uziren, and a search was started to bring them to justice. The Border Guard has been notified of the attackers in case they try to flee to Wehlen. The Workers Party of Bludia condemned the incident.
Golcondist Violence in Deyr

There have been several incidents of religious violence committed by Bludish Golcondists in Deyr. The attacks targeted members of other religious groups, resulting in injuries and property damage. The situation is concerning and warrants immediate attention from law enforcement and government officials. It is recommended that measures be taken to prevent future incidents and to address the root causes of the violence.
Deyr Under Lockdown After Arrest of WPB Leader

After the arrest of Fetih Ejall, the leader of the WPB, the Bludish populace has been rioting in Deyr, calling for an end to the unfair emergency decree. In the following protests 6 people were killed and 264 people were injured. The police moved into the city of Deyr which has now been placed under lockdown. All WPB party headquarters were raided and its members were arrested to answer for the terrorism charges.
Giralt Unveils Newest Wine and Sends Message

The famed Dandelion label of Erlory, rooted in the rich viticulture legacy of Giralt of Ribery, has introduced a new wine to its esteemed collection. Mr. Haute-Bellasorde has sent a fine selection to the Maroon Palace and wrote a little note to accompany it.

"Wine, like politics, operates not on a scale of lesser or greater, but on a spectrum of nuanced complexity. The distinctions are subjective, the flavors as variable as policy decisions. As a winemaker studies the subtle notes in each grape, a politician must examine the unique shades of each strategy. If I'm to choose between one vintage and another, between one policy and another, I'd rather not choose at all, but rather, appreciate and comprehend the intricate interplay each presents. After all, the art of winemaking, and indeed politics, lies not in forced choices but in understanding and celebrating the subtle complexities inherent within."

This latest addition is expected to uphold the characteristic floral tones, depth, and elegance that Dandelion wines are cherished for.  Wine connoisseurs and industry experts await the opportunity to savour this new vintage, and its potential influence on the Sordish wine industry is a topic of considerable interest.
Massive Network of BFF Priests Discovered

Bergian Special Zone Security has reported the discovery of a large-scale religious network of the BFF that encompasses all cities in Bergia. Under the guise of state-sanctioned priesthood, the BFF has recruited hundreds and possibly thousands of Golcondist worshippers to join the militant group and converted hundreds of Nurity worshippers to the sect of Golcondism.

A dozen arrests were made but since most police officers don't speak Bludish it will be difficult to find the actual ring leader priests of the network. Many requests were made to ban Bludish as a language from sanctuaries. Governor Bron also requested Golcondism to be banned as a religion.
Bludish Freedom Front Using Schools To Recruit And Train Militants

A school in Erzaren was discovered to be acting as a hidden facility of the Bludish Freedom Front, where they employed methods of Bludish nationalist propaganda and military training. It is suspected that the BFF has been using rural schools all around Bergia to recruit and train students for their cause. These operations are often hidden and occur mainly in areas with a majority Bludish population, where schools opt for using the Bludish language over Sordish. Many of these communities tend to struggle with the Sordish language and become easier targets for the BFF.

The situation is concerning, as it involves the indoctrination and recruitment of young individuals into a violent and extremist organization. It is recommended that the government take immediate action to prevent the Bludish Freedom Front from using schools as a tool for their recruitment efforts.
359 Arrested at Illegal Assembly

Thousands of railway construction workers from Taurus Holding went on strike at Gelsord today to protest the veto of the workers' rights bill. They violated the suspension of protests and disrupted progress on the L-1 Railway. Riot police immediately intervened and arrested 359, after a massive clash in which dozens were wounded. The situation at the site caused massive damage to the equipment.
L-1 Workers On Strike

Thousands of railway construction workers from Taurus Holding went on strike at Gelsord today disrupting progress on the L-1 Railway project. The management board of Taurus reported that they have lost control. The workers, many of whom were wearing Labour Union flags, petitioned for better working conditions and for a raise of the minimum wage. Dozens were seen holding slogans against the recent veto. Police have arrived on site to act if necessary.

The Alphonso Foundation has publicly expressed gratitude for a sizable donation from the President. This contribution bolsters the foundation's multifaceted efforts to combat homelessness and income inequality. The influx of funds is a boon to the foundation's resource pool and promises to facilitate the expansion of its existing projects and future initiatives.
Arcasia Embargo Begins

The embargo on Arcasia has come into full effect. A massive convoy of 1158 trucks accumulated at the Sodord Border Crossing close to Valgen when the border officials shut the gates. Nearly eighty percent of Arcasian trade was previously conducted through this area. Meanwhile 4507 Arcasian citizens were denied entry to the country at customs areas.

Massive economic disruptions occurred in the Gruni region. President Walker sent a direct message to the administration highlighting that this action was a grave mistake.
General Staff Commends The Administration

The general staff convened at Camp Strongarm. A session much shorter than usual concluded with a positive military analysis of Sordland's field capabilities. The Chief of the Armed Forces Valken Kruger, made a public press statement praising the administration and its efforts to strengthen the most important branch of the government, the military.

All staff generals co-signed a letter of support to the Rayne administration.
General Staff Condemns The Administration

The general staff convened at Camp Strongarm. A session much longer than usual concluded with a disastrous military analysis of Sordland's field capabilities. The Chief of the Armed Forces Valken Kruger, made a public press statement condemning the administration and its efforts to weaken the most important branch of the government, the military.

All staff generals co-signed a letter of condemnation to the Rayne administration.
Construction Problems Fixed

The Sordish State Corporation has sent a positive report outlining that the safety issues slowing down the construction have been solved due to the allocation of new funds. The doubled machinery and workers helped the SSC get back on track to finish the project on time. The Ministry of Economy also confirmed the statement.
3684 Were Taken Into Custody After Unlawfully Protesting

Over the weekend, we have taken 3684 citizens in police custody for protesting unlawfully after the passing of the emergency decree. Out of the 3684, 134 have been arrested and charged. The interrogations are still underway to learn if they have memberships to any known organisations.
Decreased Police Budget Left Police Overwhelmed

Recent decreases in the police budget has left many police headquarters all over the country overwhelmed against the recent protests. They simply do not have enough supplies to handle the riots. A help request was raised from almost every city and we are unable to provide the required supplies.
2660 Dismissed For Links To Terrorist Groups
This week, 2660 state employees were sacked for alleged links to terrorist groups under the emergency decree.
Ministry of Education Has Started Work On Education Reform

Minister of Education Ciara Walda is reporting that she has begun working on the approved education reform. The details of the education reform will be finalised over the upcoming months. If the reform package is accepted, the next steps of this process would be to discuss the indoctrination of education.
Increased Police Budget Restores Stability

Recent increases in the police budget has helped the police forces tremendously in dealing with protests all over the country. Arrests are being made swiftly and quickly while protecting the population. With the current forecast, we are expecting everything to return to normalcy very soon.
Embargo on Rumburg Enacted

The embargo on Rumburg has come into full effect. Thousands of citizens with Rumburgian nationality are being rejected at the customs areas from all points of entry. Trade between our two nations has virtually ceased.

Trains with cargo are lining up at the Albrecht Border Crossing north of Estord with several hundred thousand tons of goods unable to cross for delivery on either side of the border. Tensions are rising because oil, coal, and gas shipments bound to Rumburg were denied passage by border officials.

The Rumburg ambassador called the action an act of escalation towards war.
SSC Promised To Deliver

The official warning from the Presidency and the Ministry of Economy was received by the Sordish State Corporation. The chairman of the managers has apologised for the current situation but highlighted that rushing the work would risk real lives. The entire board signed a letter promising to meet the deadlines earlier outlined.
SSC Managers Replaced

After the recent order from the Ministry of Economy, the Sordish State Corporation has reshuffled their entire managerial board with new experts suggested by Minister Holl. The new managers are getting used to their positions and have indicated that they will do their best to meet current deadlines.
United Contana Embargoed

The embargo on United Contana has come into full effect. Our mutual trade has stopped and travellers with Contanan nationality are being denied entry into Sordland from all airports, sea ports, and border crossings. The port of Lachaven has denied 58 cargo ships from docking and unloading since the embargo began. The gulf is filled with Contanan trade ships that have anchored. This led to a major disruption of goods in Lachaven and Sordland in general.

The Embassy of United Contana made a condemning declaration calling unilateral actions like this a threat to world peace.
Crack Down on Teachers Strike

The teacher's union went on a large strike today at Republic Avenue in Lachaven to declare their opposition to the reduction in the education budget. Many displayed worry for their salaries and positions even though a suspension of protests was in place.

Riot police cracked down on the group immediately leaving several wounded. The strike ended the same day. Minister Walda gave an official statement that the strikers had a right to make their point but at home and that she is equally saddened by the developments.

Gasom, Lachaven's local energy giant, has resumed its hiring operations after several months of pause. The company recently welcomed a hundred new employees to its workforce, signaling a potential recovery phase after an extended hiring freeze. With the latest additions, Gasom looks set to rejuvenate its operations and drive towards a more robust performance in the upcoming months.

A significant shift in workforce dynamics has been announced at Gasom's Lachaven branch. In a strategic move, the energy company has declared its plan for downsizing. While this action aims at boosting the operational efficiency of the organization, it has created an atmosphere of uncertainty among the existing workforce. The effects of this decision on the local economy and Gasom's future course of action are being keenly observed.

The potential consequences of a lack of investments were highlighted. Edith Agnoc relayed that a large surplus should be utilized in further expenditures to increase the strength of the currency and the drive the recovery of the economy.

Central Bank Issues Budget Deficit Warning

The potential consequences of irresponsible economic management were highlighted. Edith Agnoc relayed that a large deficit could have dire consequences on the strength of the currency and the hamper the potential of the still to recover economy.

16 students plotting to organise a rally have been arrested by the police and taken into solitary confinement. Due to the removal of the trial process, the arrests are being made much faster and we have been able to suppress the protests quickly and decisively.

The results show that our military equipment is outdated and needs replacement as soon as possible. The continuation of the worrying report shows that in the event of an attack our border would be broken through easily, leaving the primary regions of Sordland exposed.

In a recent public statement, Prime Minister Patricio Alvarez voiced stern condemnation of Rizia's cooperative energy agreement with Sordland. Unidentified Object Spotted Close to Qinali Border

Security agencies in Morella have reported sighting an unidentified object close to the Qinali border. The object was flying at high altitude and at very high speeds. Currently, there is no clarity on what the object could be or its potential implications. Some intelligence officers indicated that the sighting could be a potential CSP low orbit satellite. 

The Morellan authorities are working with their Qinali counterparts to investigate the matter further.
Education in Rural Regions Require Improvements

Ciara Walda reports that the current education institutions in rural regions of Sordland have been largely neglected. As part of her analysis, the literacy rate in Sordland currently stands at 80% while rural regions like Narbel has a literacy rate of only 64%. The lack of schools per capita also reflects these results.
Rizia Hails Energy Collaboration Success

Following the successful joint investment in Gasom, King Romus praised the initiative as a model of regional cooperation. He emphasized its potential to inspire future partnerships aimed at achieving mutual economic growth. The King also expressed confidence in the continued expansion of ROG and the sustainability of this collaborative approach to energy investments.
Queen Beatrice Livingston Calls Sordland a Threat to World Peace

Queen Beatrice Livingston appeared on TV to call Sordland not just a threat to peace in Eastern Merkopa but a threat to peace in the entire world.

She has also publicly condemned President Anton Rayne’s new policies and also she expressed her worries about the direction Sordland is headed. She urged the Rumburgian Army to secure the southern border, citing violent incidents in northern Sordland.

The Gruni Rural Development Plan, a brainchild of Rural Development Minister Gus Manger, is nearing completion in Holsord. This strategy aims to revitalize the rural economy, fortify food security, and enhance the regional economy of Gruni. The upcoming presentation of the finalized plan marks a significant milestone in the evolution of Sordland's rural development agenda.

Money Is Meant To Be Spent

First rule of making money is to never hold onto it. This is always a principle that holds true. However, currently Sordland seems to be doing the exact opposite.

If we want to get out of recession, we need to spend the surplus on infrastructure, projects, investments and trade. These ventures serve only to raise Sordland’s standing globally and bring in even more investments. If we come to a stand still, the recession will not go anywhere.

With certainty, conservative spending of the budget does more harm than good.
Balanced Energy Prices

Energy prices in Sordland have remained remarkably stable over the last quarter, a positive sign for our economy. With a marginal increase of 0.8%, the stability in energy prices demonstrates the resilience of our domestic energy sector amidst global market uncertainties. This stable trend offers predictability for both businesses and consumers, fostering a conducive environment for steady economic growth.
Fluctuating Energy Prices

The energy market in Sordland is experiencing a period of intense fluctuation. Over the past three months, the average price per kilowatt-hour has seen peaks and troughs ranging from a worrying high of 12% to a relieving low of -8%. These unpredictable swings can have considerable impact on the economy, affecting everything from business costs to consumer spending.
Energy Prices Skyrocket

In a worrying economic development, energy prices across Sordland have hit a record high. Data from the National Energy Board shows a sharp increase of 18% in the last quarter, triggering alarm bells among economists and policymakers. This surge could lead to higher inflation and squeeze the budgets of both households and businesses. 

The government and energy companies like Gasom will need to devise strategic interventions to tackle this looming crisis.
A Game Changer?

News of international interest in Gasom continues to spread, as reports confirm that Anraka and Qinal, alongside Galmland, are also considering significant investments. This potential injection of foreign capital could drastically alter the financial landscape of the struggling Sordish energy giant, promising a potential turnaround. 

As proponents of free market economics, we must welcome such investments as opportunities, rather than threats.
Bankruptcy Looms Over Gasom

Sordland's energy giant Gasom stands on shaky financial ground, with bankruptcy a real possibility. The company has struggled to cope with market instability and changing regulations, leading to a sharp decline in its fiscal health. This potential collapse poses serious implications for Sordland's energy sector and broader economy.
Downsizing Marks a New Era for Gasom

Gasom has announced a series of downsizing measures in an attempt to stabilize its financial health. While this development presents a challenging landscape for the company, it could potentially serve as a catalyst for reform and renewal.
Rizia's Investment: A Lifeline for Gasom

Rizia's investment in Gasom provides a critical lifeline for the struggling Sordish energy giant. This infusion of capital offers a path toward recovery and financial stability, demonstrating the tangible benefits of international cooperation in the energy sector. The move reflects how strategic partnerships can create opportunities for revitalizing key industries.

This development is expected to positively influence Sordland's energy landscape, potentially spurring economic growth and enhancing the nation’s competitiveness on the global stage.
Royal Emerald Energy Eyes Gasom - A Strategic Move?

Rumburg's Royal Emerald Energy's potential investment in Sordland's Gasom is a move to be welcomed, not feared. This could be the lifeline that Gasom, a bedrock of our domestic energy sector, needs to recover from its financial difficulties. While concerns about foreign ownership are understandable, the international dynamics of free market economies must be recognized.

Economy Slowly Recovering

Manufacturers cranked up the assembly lines again and many businesses welcomed back customers.
Economy Slowly Recovering

After all, large corporations bring in more money into Sordland and they are the reason the recession is not worse than it already is. This decision will definitely benefit Sordland in the long run.

We can’t help but question President Rayne’s real intentions with this decision.

The ship entered the area without Valgslandian Navy's prior permission, they said. ‘The illegal occupation of Heljiland does not give Agnolia the right to claim the seas. Our stance has been that if you do anything in our region, you have to notify us or take our permission,’ the Navy Chief said at a press conference without elaborating further on the incident.

Progress on Iyotake Plan Boosts Nibiya and Surrounding Nations

The ambitious Iyotake Plan, led by the astute Vice-Secretary Chairman Toqezintli Iyotake, continues its march in Nibiya and has expanded its influence into neighboring nations such as Zaerland, East Dorghuk, Sonsamia, and beyond. Despite facing a myriad of controversies and the inherent challenges of implementing vast socio-economic transformations, the CSP's propagandist agenda is undeniably poised to determine Rika's trajectory.

The unfolding dynamics present a pressing query: How will the ATO counter such an extensive geopolitical maneuver? The chessboard is set, and the game's stakes are high, potentially defining the ideological alignment of Rika for decades to come.
Prime Minister Alvarez of Lespia Visits Pales, Offers Support Amid Tensions with Rizia

In a show of solidarity, Prime Minister Alvarez of Lespia visited the Grand Duchy of Pales and its leader, Axel Reinhart, to affirm Lespia's support in the face of mounting pressure from Rizia over the disputed gas fields. As part of the ATO alliance, Lespia has offered assistance to Pales in resolving the ongoing gas field dispute and maintaining regional stability.

He also pledged Lespia's commitment to defending Pales' sovereignty and territorial integrity if the dispute were to escalate.

The visit has sent a strong message to Rizia, warning them against further aggressive actions and encouraging a diplomatic resolution to the dispute. However, it remains to be seen whether Rizia will accept these proposals and engage in dialogue with Pales and Lespia to reach a peaceful settlement.
Arcasian PMCs Accused of Sowing Discord in Eastern Xina

President Soll demonstrated unexpected warmth yesterday when he invited local fishermen into his Duru Island residence for afternoon tea. The casual gathering offered a rare glimpse into the private life of the typically reserved statesman.

President Anton Rayne's recent massive donation to the Alphonso Foundation has stirred up controversy. While the act may appear philanthropic on the surface, it serves to distract from the real issue at hand - the deep-rooted income inequality in Sordland. Pouring money into foundations named after former Presidents does not absolve the current administration of its responsibility to address these systemic disparities directly. 

We need tangible change, not just symbolic gestures.
Demonstrators Arrested

Tens of thousands of demonstrators were driven out from city centres by riot police in the week. According to ground sources, thousands have been detained. The government has still not declared the real numbers or the identities of the individuals.

The government crackdown on the protests around the country was swift and brought an end to the chaos in major cities such as Holsord and Lachaven. Reports from mayors around the country came in today, saying that the protests are under control and stability will return.
Pro-Rayne Purge

Thousands of state employees were dismissed under the emergency decree for alleged links to subversive groups. So far under the decree, 12,662 people, including nearly 1,000 police officers, and hundreds of teachers and academics were sacked.

The opposition leader, Mr. Ricter said Sordland was now entering a dangerous period of ‘totalist rule’.

Arcasia and Lespia have also accused the president of using the Bernard Circas’ murder as an excuse to crack down on dissent.
Red Youth Calls For Peace

Earlier today, Johan Gasmich, one of the leaders of the Red Youth, spoke to the public and condemned the ‘opportunistic’ looting and violence taking place in cities across Sordland, saying it is not being done in the name of Bernard Circas.

He denied ‘terrorist’ allegations and condemned the attacks, saying that Red Youth has no connection to the violence. He accused the police of trying to sway the public opinion against socialism and legal Malenyevist groups such as the Red Youth.

‘Some people are trying to incite violence and take away the meaning of these peaceful protests,’ said Gasmich, warning the protesters about inside people trying to exploit the situation. He also called for peace, saying that the ‘justified and meaningful protests have already lost their course and started benefitting a select group of people.’
Charity or Camouflage? President's Donation Scrutinized

With a trail of socio-economic discrepancies strewn over his tenure, former President Alphonso might think that the establishment of the Alphonso Foundation is sufficient to absolve him of past transgressions. However, this recently received presidential seal of approval via a hefty donation does little more than highlight the ongoing stratification of wealth in Sordland. 

President Anton Rayne's small contribution to the Foundation is nothing short of a misdirected resource allocation, acting as a smokescreen for the glaring income inequality brought about by the economic liberalization policies of 'Alphonsonomics'. This attempt to brush over systemic issues with charitable acts is perceived as nothing more than a classic case of millionaire power-play.
President Rayne, the USP and the Colonel

On Friday morning, President Rayne and Education Minister Walda visited a middle school in Leiren. Known to be a proudly Sollist establishment, Toren Hill School is one of the most popular middle schools in Sordland.

During the visit, the President was seen speaking with the pupils and school staff before he ordered the removal of Tarquin Soll’s portrait from the building. The reasoning behind this controversial and brave move still stands as an unknown, but it will surely create problems for President Rayne with his own party.

This event might have very well been just for show, or a sign that there are widening cracks between President Rayne and the USP. Or is this a sign that the USP is finally feeling the pressure and opting for a change in their values? Whatever the case might be, the foundations of the USP and the cult figure of Tarquin Soll seems to be losing its strength.

President’s Display of Incompetence

President’s move to veto the Worker’s Rights Act has caused the construction that he himself started to come to a halt due to the rightful strikes of the Taurus Holding workers. These people have spent months working in dire conditions for pennies.

This decision of the administration not to give these people at least a minimum wage, proper safety regulation and overtime pay only shows the President's incompetence but also the lack of understanding of the consequences for his actions.

As a nation we are undergoing trials under our new president, mostly caused by Mr. Rayne sitting on his chair comfortably and not feeling the pulse of the country.
Rayne Attacks Small And Medium Businesses

When will this end? The Ministry of Economy has just announced a tax increase for small/medium corporations bringing the total to 45%. President Rayne’s priorities are now crystal clear.

Instead of siding with his people, he decided to target and attack smaller corporations to make his gains to supposedly end the recession. How will this end the recession? The answer is: It won’t.

The real question we all need to ask is what is Rayne getting out of it?
Rayne Is The New Toy of Oligarchs

When will this end? The Ministry of Economy has just announced a tax increase for small/medium corporations bringing the total to 45% AND tax cuts for large corporations bringing the total to 25%. President Rayne’s priorities are now crystal clear.

Instead of siding with his people, he decided to open his welcoming arms to large corporations and the oligarchs while some of his citizens still to this date suffer from starvation. He has declared his intention was to end the recession. That’s a lie.

The real question is what is he getting out of it? Who bribed the President so that he ended up laying in the same bed with large corporations?

I am very worried about the future of Sordland and until President Rayne leaves his chair, we, The Radical, will not rest.
Workers Rights Bill Signed

In a surprising move, President Rayne has decided to do something right for his citizens by signing the Worker’s Rights Act into a law.

This looks as a publicity move after the terrible Morbel Mine Disaster. The new law establishes a minimum wage and sets a ceiling for the maximum amount of hours on top of new regulations for companies. Mr. Rayne’s move to give more rights to the workers has been welcomed by many.

On the other hand, this may simply be a diversion from the actual real issues of the government.
No Empathy for the Working Class

The Assembly which has so many different opinions came together to present a bill in the hopes of improving the labour rights in Sordland but President Rayne has shown no empathy for the struggles of the workers.

The veto is a sign that the administration doesn't care as much for the average citizen of the country as I had hoped. The mine disaster was a tragic but good example why improved and safer working conditions must be upheld. These subjects are about human lives and their happiness.

The priority must stay with the people. The very factor that will re-elect or choose someone else come 1957.

BFF Warns Wehlen, Sordland and Lespia

In a startling announcement, spokespersons of the Bludish Freedom Front (BFF) have released a statement condemning the governments of Sordland, Lespia, and Wehlen for their mistreatment of Bludish citizens. The statement warns of potential action against these governments if they continue to ignore the will of the Bludish people.

The BFF statement particularly targets the government of Wehlen, accusing President Wiktor Smolak of planning to carry out a genocide against the Bludish people. These shocking allegations demand immediate attention and action from the international community to prevent such atrocities.

It is high time for these governments to listen to the voices of their Bludish citizens and respect their rights and freedoms, otherwise militant groups like the BFF will take the lead and push the region into violence.
